const j = JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(0,'utf-8'))
const types = j.root.children.map((c,i) => {
  let info = c.type
  if (c.type === 'heading') info += '(' + c.tag + '): ' + (c.children?.[0]?.text || '')
  else if (c.type === 'details') info += ': ' + (c.summary || '').slice(0, 30)
  else if (c.type === 'paragraph') info += ': ' + (c.children?.map(ch => ch.text || ch.type || '').join('') || '').slice(0, 40)
  else if (c.type === 'list') info += '(' + c.listType + ', ' + c.children.length + ' items)'
  else if (c.type === 'table') info += '(' + c.children.length + ' rows)'
  else if (c.type === 'quote') info += ': ' + (c.children?.[0]?.children?.[0]?.text || '').slice(0, 40)
  else if (c.type === 'image') info += ': ' + c.altText
  else if (c.type === 'link-card') info += ': ' + c.url
  return '  [' + i + '] ' + info
})
console.log('Total nodes:', j.root.children.length)
console.log(types.join('\n'))
"
```

     ```typescript
     export class TagNode extends DecoratorNode<ReactElement> {
       __text: string;
       static getType(): string {
         return 'tag';
       }
       static clone(node: TagNode): TagNode {
         return new TagNode(node.__text, node.__key);
       }
       constructor(text: string, key?: NodeKey) {
         super(key);
         this.__text = text;
       }
       isInline(): boolean {
         return true;
       }
       static importJSON(serializedNode: SerializedTagNode): TagNode {
         return $createTagNode(serializedNode.text);
       }
       exportJSON(): SerializedTagNode {
         return { ...super.exportJSON(), type: 'tag', text: this.__text, version: 1 };
       }
       decorate(_editor: LexicalEditor, _config: EditorConfig): ReactElement {
         return createRendererDecoration('Tag', TagRenderer, { text: this.__text });
       }
     }
     export function $createTagNode(text: string): TagNode {
       return new TagNode(text);
     }
     export function $isTagNode(node: LexicalNode | null | undefined): node is TagNode {

     }

   336→  const src: string = n.url ?? ''
   337→  const alt: string = n.alt ?? ''
   338→  const title: string | undefined = n.title || undefined
   339→
   340→  // Video extension detection
   341→  if (VIDEO_EXTS.test(src)) return video(src)
   342→
   343→  return image(src, alt, title)
   344→}
   345→
   346→// ── Table ──
   347→
   348→function convertTable(n: any, pre: PreprocessResult): LNode {
   349→  const rows: LNode[] = []
   350→  for (let i = 0; i < (n.children ?? []).length; i++) {
   351→    const row = n.children[i] as any
   352→    const cells: LNode[] = []
   353→    for (const cell of row.children ?? []) {
   354→      // headerState: 1 for header row (first row), 0 otherwise
   355→      const hs = i === 0 ? 1 : 0
   356→      const cellChildren = convertInlineChildren(cell.children ?? [], pre)
   357→      cells.push(tableCell(hs, paragraph(...cellChildren)))
   358→    }
   359→    rows.push(tableRow(...cells))
   360→  }
   361→  return tableNode(...rows)
   362→}
   363→
   364→// ── HTML nodes ──
   365→
   366→function convertHtml(html: string, pre: PreprocessResult): LNode | LNode[] | null {
   367→  const trimmed = html.trim()
   368→
   369→  // Check for our placeholders (HTML comments)
   370→  if (PLACEHOLDER_RE.test(trimmed)) {
   371→    // Try container map first, then html map
   372→    const containerBlock = pre.containers.get(trimmed)
   373→    if (containerBlock) return convertContainer(containerBlock, pre)
   374→    const htmlBlock = pre.htmlBlocks.get(trimmed)
   375→    if (htmlBlock) return convertHtmlBlock(htmlBlock, pre)
   376→  }
   377→
   378→  // <video src="..." /> or <video src="..."></video>
   379→  const videoMatch = trimmed.match(/<video[^>]*\bsrc=["']([^"']+)["'][^>]*\/?>/i)
   380→  if (videoMatch) return video(videoMatch[1])
   381→
   382→  // <tag>text</tag>
   383→  const tagMatch = trimmed.match(/^<tag>([^<]+)<\/tag>$/i)
   384→  if (tagMatch) return { type: 'tag', text: tagMatch[1], version: 1 }
   385→
   386→  // <ruby>
   387→  const rubyMatch = trimmed.match(/^<ruby>([^<]*)<rt>([^<]*)<\/rt>(?:<rp>[^<]*<\/rp>)*<\/ruby>$/i)
   388→  if (rubyMatch) return { type: 'ruby', reading: rubyMatch[2], children: [text(rubyMatch[1])], direction: 'ltr', format: '', indent: 0, version: 1 }
   389→
   390→  return null
   391→}
   392→
   393→function convertHtmlBlock(
   394→  block: { tag: string; attrs: Record<string, string>; content: string },
   395→  pre: PreprocessResult,
   396→): LNode | null {
   397→  switch (block.tag) {
   398→    case 'details': {
   399→      // content starts with <summary>...</summary>
   400→      const sumMatch = block.content.match(/^<summary>([\s\S]*?)<\/summary>\s*([\s\S]*)$/i)
   401→      const summary = sumMatch ? sumMatch[1].trim() : ''
   402→      const bodyMd = sumMatch ? sumMatch[2].trim() : block.content
   403→      // Recursively convert the body markdown
   404→      const bodyNodes = convertMarkdownString(bodyMd, pre)
   405→      const isOpen = 'open' in block.attrs
   406→      return details(summary, isOpen, ...bodyNodes)
   407→    }
   408→
   409→    case 'tabs': {
   410→      // Parse <tab label="...">content</tab> blocks
   411→      const tabRegex = /<tab\s+label=["']([^"']+)["']\s*>([\s\S]*?)<\/tab>/gi
   412→      const files: { filename: string; language: string; code: string }[] = []
   413→      let m: RegExpExecArray | null
   414→      while ((m = tabRegex.exec(block.content)) !== null) {
   415→        const label = m[1]
   416→        const tabContent = m[2].trim()
   417→        // Try to extract code block from tab content
   418→        const codeMatch = tabContent.match(/^```(\w*)\n([\s\S]*?)\n```$/)
   419→        if (codeMatch) {
   420→          files.push({ filename: label, language: codeMatch[1] || '', code: codeMatch[2] })
   421→        } else {
   422→          files.push({ filename: label, language: '', code: tabContent })
   423→        }
   424→      }
   425→      if (files.length > 0) return codeSnippet(files)
   426→      return null
   427→    }
   428→
   429→    case 'excalidraw':
   430→      return excalidraw(block.content)
   431→
   432→    case 'nested-doc': {
   433→      const bodyNodes = convertMarkdownString(block.content, pre)
   434→      return nestedDoc(...bodyNodes)
   435→    }
   436→
   437→    default:
   438→      return null
   439→  }
   440→}
   441→
   442→// ── Container blocks ──
   443→
   444→function convertContainer(block: ContainerBlock, pre: PreprocessResult): LNode | null {
   445→  const typeMap: Record<string, string> = {
   446→    warning: 'warn',
   447→    danger: 'error',
   448→    note: 'info',
   449→  }
   450→
   451→  switch (block.type) {
   452→    case 'gallery':
   453→    case 'carousel': {
   454→      const images = pickImages(block.content)
   455→      return gallery(images, block.type === 'carousel' ? 'carousel' : 'grid')
   456→    }
   457→
   458→    case 'masonry': {
   459→      const images = pickImages(block.content)
   460→      return gallery(images, 'masonry')
   461→    }
   462→
   463→    case 'banner': {
   464→      const bannerType = block.params || 'info'
   465→      const bodyNodes = convertMarkdownString(block.content, pre)
   466→      return banner(typeMap[bannerType] || bannerType, ...bodyNodes)
   467→    }
   468→
   469→    case 'warn':
   470→    case 'error':
   471→    case 'danger':
   472→    case 'info':
   473→    case 'success':
   474→    case 'warning':
   475→    case 'note': {
   476→      const mappedType = typeMap[block.type] || block.type
   477→      const bodyNodes = convertMarkdownString(block.content, pre)
   478→      return banner(mappedType, ...bodyNodes)
   479→    }
   480→
   481→    case 'details': {
   482→      const params = parseContainerParams(block.params)
   483→      const summary = params.summary?.replace(/^"|"$/g, '') ?? ''
   484→      const bodyNodes = convertMarkdownString(block.content, pre)
   485→      return details(summary, false, ...bodyNodes)
   486→    }
   487→
   488→    case 'grid': {
   489→      const params = parseContainerParams(block.params)
   490→      const cols = Number.parseInt(params.cols ?? '2', 10)
   491→      const rawGap = params.gap?.replace(/^"|"$/g, '') ?? '16px'
   492→      const gap = /\d+$/.test(rawGap) ? `${rawGap}px` : rawGap
   493→
   494→      if (params.type === 'images') {
   495→        const images = pickImages(block.content)
   496→        return gallery(images, 'grid')
   497→      }
   498→
   499→      // Split content by ::: cell markers into separate cells
   500→      const cellParts = block.content.split(/^\s*::: *cell\s*$/gm).filter((s) => s.trim())
   501→      // Remove trailing ::: from each cell
   502→      const cells = cellParts.map((part) => {
   503→        const cleaned = part.replace(/^\s*:::\s*$/gm, '').trim()
   504→        return wrapRoot(convertMarkdownString(cleaned, pre))
   505→      })
   506→      if (cells.length === 0) {
   507→        const bodyNodes = convertMarkdownString(block.content, pre)
   508→        cells.push(wrapRoot(bodyNodes))
   509→      }
   510→      return gridContainer(cols, gap, cells)
   511→    }
   512→
   513→    default:
   514→      return null
   515→  }
   516→}
   517→
   518→// ── Helpers ──
   519→
   520→function pickImages(content: string): { src: string; alt?: string }[] {
   521→  const regex = /!\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]+)\)/g
   522→  const images: { src: string; alt?: string }[] = []
   523→  let m: RegExpExecArray | null
   524→  while ((m = regex.exec(content)) !== null) {
   525→    images.push({ src: m[2], alt: m[1] || undefined })
   526→  }
   527→  return images
   528→}
   529→
   530→function parseContainerParams(params: string): Record<string, string> {
   531→  const result: Record<string, string> = {}
   532→  const regex = /(\w+)=(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)'|(\S+))/g
   533→  let m: RegExpExecArray | null
   534→  while ((m = regex.exec(params)) !== null) {
   535→    result[m[1]] = m[2] ?? m[3] ?? m[4]
   536→  }
   537→  return result
   538→}
   539→
   540→function collectFootnoteDefinitions(root: MdastNode): Record<string, string> {
   541→  const defs: Record<string, string> = {}
   542→  const r = root as any
   543→  if (!r.children) return defs
   544→  for (const child of r.children) {
   545→    if (child.type === 'footnoteDefinition') {
   546→      defs[child.identifier ?? ''] = toString(child)
   547→    }
   548→  }
   549→  return defs
   550→}
   551→
   552→function convertMarkdownString(md: string, _parentPre: PreprocessResult): LNode[] {
   553→  // Re-preprocess nested content to handle inner containers/HTML blocks
   554→  const subPre = preprocess(md)
   555→  const subAst = parseMarkdown(subPre.processed)
   556→  const subResult = markdownToLexical(subAst, subPre)
   557→  return subResult.root.children
   558→}

import * as fs from 'fs'
const json = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('/dev/stdin', 'utf8'))
const root = json.root.children

// Count details nodes
let detailsCount = 0
function walk(node: any, depth = 0) {
  if (node.type === 'details') {
    detailsCount++
    console.log('DETAILS #' + detailsCount + ': summary=' + JSON.stringify(node.summary))
  }
  if (node.children) node.children.forEach((c: any) => walk(c, depth + 1))
}
root.forEach((n: any) => walk(n))
console.log('Total details:', detailsCount)

// Find raw == in text nodes
let rawEqCount = 0
function findRawEq(node: any, path = '') {
  if (node.text && typeof node.text === 'string' && node.text.includes('==')) {
    rawEqCount++
    console.log('RAW == at', path, ':', JSON.stringify(node.text).slice(0, 80))
  }
  if (node.children) node.children.forEach((c: any, i: number) => findRawEq(c, path + '/' + i))
}
console.log('\\n--- Raw == text nodes ---')
root.forEach((n: any, i: number) => findRawEq(n, '/' + i))
console.log('Total raw == nodes:', rawEqCount)

// Count highlighted text nodes
let highlightCount = 0
function findHighlight(node: any) {
  if (node.type === 'text' && (node.format & 128)) {
    highlightCount++
  }
  if (node.children) node.children.forEach((c: any) => findHighlight(c))
}
root.forEach((n: any) => findHighlight(n))
console.log('\\nHighlighted text nodes:', highlightCount)
" 2> /dev/null
```

==**内向&社恐**==，从小以来不擅长于他人交往，性格孤僻。因为从小与计算机结缘，特别热衷于计算机领域，从而失去了童年应该于其他小孩子一起玩耍的天性。最后造成了话题只局限于计算机领域，导致了交际能力弱，不擅长交流。即便是年龄的增长，也不知道自己的说的话对不对，无意间触碰到别人的感受。至此还是少说话为妙。“有社交恐惧的人其实不少是渴望和人交流的，但是他们怕尴尬，或者被伤害到，被看不起。当你打开了有社交恐惧的人的心结，当他们敞开心扉了，他们能比话痨还话痨。”

==**沉思者**==，失落的时候总是能把思绪放到未来，感概未来，我却一事无成。是一个比较悲观的人，不会鼓励自己，却想着鼓励别人的反面人。高中阶段，开小差时往往会思考人生。

==**某种意义上的赶时髦者**==，穿搭打扮毫无要求，只是在编程领域，反对过时特性，反对各种风格混搭派，追求现代设计风，喜欢自我设计，但却是个 UI 设计初心者。

==**处于亚健康的体弱多病**==，从小不爱玩耍导致从小学以来体育一直处于班里倒数阶段，初中时期为了应付体育中考，是人生中体育体制巅峰期。大学时期一直处于废柴状态。患有某种以现代医学无法根治的皮肤病。哀

==**简洁主义者**==，花里胡哨厌倦者，认为生活就应该简简单单，必要的生活物品，以及恰饭工具即可。简单即知足。

==**某种意义上的换位思考者**==，以开发者的身份，站在普通用户的角度体验自己开发的东西，是否有存在的必要性，是否拥有良好的体验感，是否需要附加功能。

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Now I see the issue. The small details blocks (Innei, 拾一, 寻, 亿夏) have their content entirely in HTML (`<p>`, `<span class="spoiler">`, `<blockquote>`), not in markdown. The `convertHtmlBlock` function does:

```typescript
case 'details': {
  const sumMatch = block.content.match(/^<summary>([\s\S]*?)<\/summary>\s*([\s\S]*)$/i)
  const summary = sumMatch ? sumMatch[1].trim() : ''
  const bodyMd = sumMatch ? sumMatch[2].trim() : block.content
  const bodyNodes = convertMarkdownString(bodyMd, pre)
  const isOpen = 'open' in block.attrs
  return details(summary, isOpen, ...bodyNodes)
}
```

It extracts the summary, then tries to convert the remaining body as markdown. But the body is HTML like:

```html
<p class="paragraph">
  <span class="spoiler">来源于罗马音...</span>
</p>
```

When this is passed to `convertMarkdownString`, remark parses it as a single HTML block (since it's all HTML tags), and `convertHtml` doesn't know how to handle `<p>` tags directly—it only handles specific elements like `<blockquote>` and `<img>`.

So I need to handle the HTML body content properly. The body can contain paragraphs with spoiler spans, blockquotes, and markdown formatting inside spoilers. Rather than trying to extend `convertHtml` to handle every tag, I should convert the HTML to markdown first, then pass it through the existing markdown converter. That way `<p class="paragraph"><span class="spoiler">text</span></p>` becomes `||text||`, and `<blockquote>` becomes a markdown quote block, which the markdown parser already knows how to handle. I need to handle `<strong>` tags as well, converting them to markdown bold. Rather than parsing HTML directly into Lexical nodes, I'll create an `htmlToMarkdown` helper that converts the HTML body to markdown first, then pass it through `convertMarkdownString` in the `convertHtmlBlock` function.

</details></think>

The blockquote line starts with spaces (`    > ==...==`). The leading spaces cause remark to interpret it as a code block (4 spaces = indented code block in CommonMark). The `> ` needs to start at column 1.

The issue is in the `htmlBodyToMarkdown` function. The blockquote regex captures the inner content including leading whitespace from each line, then `trim()` + `split('\n')` processes it. But the outer indentation from the original HTML remains in the result because the replacement includes the surrounding whitespace.

Wait, looking again at the output:```

```

The problem is that the original HTML has indentation before the `<blockquote>` tag itself, and that indentation is preserved in the final output even though the regex only replaces the tag content. The surrounding whitespace from the HTML structure isn't being stripped away.

The simplest solution is to dedent the entire result at the end, removing leading whitespace from each line.

<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```typescript
import sharp from 'sharp';
import { rgbaToThumbHash } from 'thumbhash';

import type { LNode } from './types.js';

interface ImageMeta {
  width: number;
  height: number;
  thumbhash: string;
  accent: string;
}

const cache = new Map<string, ImageMeta | null>();

async function fetchImageBuffer(src: string): Promise<Buffer | null> {
  try {
    if (src.startsWith('http://') || src.startsWith('https://')) {
      const res = await fetch(src, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) });
      if (!res.ok) return null;
      return Buffer.from(await res.arrayBuffer());
    }
    // Local file
    const { readFileSync } = await import('node:fs');
    return readFileSync(src);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

async function computeMeta(src: string): Promise<ImageMeta | null> {
  if (cache.has(src)) return cache.get(src)!;

  const buf = await fetchImageBuffer(src);
  if (!buf) {
    cache.set(src, null);
    return null;
  }

  try {
    const img = sharp(buf);
    const metadata = await img.metadata();
    const width = metadata.width!;
    const height = metadata.height!;

    // Resize to small dimensions for thumbhash (max 100px)
    const thumbSize = 100;
    const { data, info } = await img
      .resize(thumbSize, thumbSize, { fit: 'inside' })
      .ensureAlpha()
      .raw()
      .toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });

    const thumbhash = Buffer.from(rgbaToThumbHash(info.width, info.height, data)).toString(
      'base64',
    );

    // Dominant color via sharp stats
    const stats = await sharp(buf).resize(1, 1).raw().toBuffer();
    const accent = `#${stats[0].toString(16).padStart(2, '0')}${stats[1].toString(16).padStart(2, '0')}${stats[2].toString(16).padStart(2, '0')}`;

    const meta: ImageMeta = { width, height, thumbhash, accent };
    cache.set(src, meta);
    return meta;
  } catch {
    cache.set(src, null);
    return null;
  }
}

function collectImageNodes(node: any, result: any[]): void {
  if (node.type === 'image' && node.src) {
    result.push(node);
  }
  if (node.children) {
    for (const child of node.children) {
      collectImageNodes(child, result);
    }
  }
  // Gallery images stored in an `images` array
  if (node.images && Array.isArray(node.images)) {
    for (const img of node.images) {
      if (img.src) result.push(img);
    }
  }
}

export async function enrichImages(root: LNode): Promise<void> {
  const imageNodes: any[] = [];
  collectImageNodes(root, imageNodes);

  if (imageNodes.length === 0) return;

  const uniqueSrcs = [...new Set(imageNodes.map((n) => n.src as string))];
  process.stderr.write(`Fetching metadata for ${uniqueSrcs.length} images...\n`);

  // Fetch in parallel with concurrency limit
  const concurrency = 5;
  for (let i = 0; i < uniqueSrcs.length; i += concurrency) {
    const batch = uniqueSrcs.slice(i, i + concurrency);
    await Promise.all(batch.map((src) => computeMeta(src)));
    process.stderr.write(
      `  ${Math.min(i + concurrency, uniqueSrcs.length)}/${uniqueSrcs.length}\n`,
    );
  }

  // Apply metadata to all image nodes
  for (const node of imageNodes) {
    const meta = cache.get(node.src);
    if (meta) {
      node.width = meta.width;
      node.height = meta.height;
      node.thumbhash = meta.thumbhash;
      node.accent = meta.accent;
    }
  }
}
```

     1→const getRandomColor = (
     2→  lightness: [number, number],
     3→  saturation: [number, number],
     4→  hue: number,
     5→) => {
     6→  const satAccent = Math.floor(
     7→    Math.random() * (saturation[1] - saturation[0] + 1) + saturation[0],
     8→  )
     9→  const lightAccent = Math.floor(
    10→    Math.random() * (lightness[1] - lightness[0] + 1) + lightness[0],
    11→  )
    12→
    13→  // Generate the background color by increasing the lightness and decreasing the saturation
    14→  const satBackground = satAccent > 30 ? satAccent - 30 : 0
    15→  const lightBackground = lightAccent < 80 ? lightAccent + 20 : 100
    16→
    17→  return {
    18→    accent: `hsl(${hue}, ${satAccent}%, ${lightAccent}%)`,
    19→    background: `hsl(${hue}, ${satBackground}%, ${lightBackground}%)`,
    20→  }
    21→}
    22→
    23→export function stringToHue(str: string) {
    24→  let hash = 0
    25→  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    26→    hash = str.charCodeAt(i) + ((hash << 5) - hash)
    27→  }
    28→  const hue = hash % 360
    29→  return hue < 0 ? hue + 360 : hue
    30→}
    31→
    32→export const getColorScheme = (hue?: number) => {
    33→  const baseHue = hue ?? Math.floor(Math.random() * 361)
    34→  const complementaryHue = (baseHue + 180) % 360
    35→
    36→  // For light theme, we limit the lightness between 40 and 70 to avoid too bright colors for accent
    37→  const lightColors = getRandomColor([40, 70], [70, 90], baseHue)
    38→
    39→  // For dark theme, we limit the lightness between 20 and 50 to avoid too dark colors for accent
    40→  const darkColors = getRandomColor([20, 50], [70, 90], complementaryHue)
    41→
    42→  return {
    43→    light: {
    44→      accent: lightColors.accent,
    45→      background: lightColors.background,
    46→    },
    47→    dark: {
    48→      accent: darkColors.accent,
    49→      background: darkColors.background,
    50→    },
    51→  }
    52→}
    53→export function addAlphaToHex(hex: string, alpha: number): string {
    54→  if (!/^#(?:[\da-f]{3}){1,2}$/i.test(hex)) {
    55→    throw new Error('Invalid hex color value')
    56→  }
    57→
    58→  let color = ''
    59→  if (hex.length === 4) {
    60→    color = `#${[1, 2, 3]
    61→      .map(
    62→        (index) =>
    63→          Number.parseInt(hex.charAt(index), 16).toString(16) +
    64→          Number.parseInt(hex.charAt(index), 16).toString(16),
    65→      )
    66→      .join('')}`
    67→  } else {
    68→    color = hex
    69→  }
    70→
    71→  const r = Number.parseInt(color.slice(1, 3), 16)
    72→  const g = Number.parseInt(color.slice(3, 5), 16)
    73→  const b = Number.parseInt(color.slice(5, 7), 16)
    74→
    75→  return `rgba(${r},${g},${b},${alpha})`
    76→}
    77→
    78→export function addAlphaToHSL(hsl: string, alpha: number): string {
    79→  if (!/^hsl\(\d{1,3}(?:,\s*[\d.]+%){2}\)$/.test(hsl)) {
    80→    throw new Error('Invalid HSL color value')
    81→  }
    82→
    83→  const hsla = `${hsl.slice(0, -1)}, ${alpha})`
    84→  return hsla.replace('hsl', 'hsla')
    85→}
    86→
    87→export function hexToHsl(hex: string) {
    88→  // Remove the '#' symbol from the hex code
    89→  hex = hex.replace('#', '')
    90→
    91→  // Convert hex values to RGB
    92→  const r = Number.parseInt(hex.slice(0, 2), 16) / 255
    93→  const g = Number.parseInt(hex.slice(2, 4), 16) / 255
    94→  const b = Number.parseInt(hex.slice(4, 6), 16) / 255
    95→
    96→  // Find the minimum and maximum values among R, G, and B
    97→  const min = Math.min(r, g, b)
    98→  const max = Math.max(r, g, b)
    99→
   100→  // Calculate the hue
   101→  let h = 0
   102→  switch (max) {
   103→    case min: {
   104→      h = 0 // No hue for achromatic colors
   105→
   106→      break
   107→    }
   108→    case r: {
   109→      h = ((g - b) / (max - min)) % 6
   110→
   111→      break
   112→    }
   113→    case g: {
   114→      h = (2 + (b - r) / (max - min)) % 6
   115→
   116→      break
   117→    }
   118→    default: {
   119→      h = (4 + (r - g) / (max - min)) % 6
   120→    }
   121→  }
   122→  h = Math.round(h * 60)
   123→
   124→  // Calculate the lightness
   125→  const l = (max + min) / 2
   126→
   127→  // Calculate the saturation
   128→  let s = 0
   129→  if (max !== min) {
   130→    s = (max - min) / (1 - Math.abs(2 * l - 1))
   131→  }
   132→  s = Math.round(s * 100)
   133→
   134→  // Return the HSL values as a string
   135→  return [h, s, Math.round(l * 100)]
   136→}
   137→
   138→export function generateTransitionColors(
   139→  startColor: string,
   140→  targetColor: string,
   141→  step: number,
   142→): string[] {
   143→  // Convert startColor and targetColor to RGB values
   144→  const startRed = Number.parseInt(startColor.slice(1, 3), 16)
   145→  const startGreen = Number.parseInt(startColor.slice(3, 5), 16)
   146→  const startBlue = Number.parseInt(startColor.slice(5, 7), 16)
   147→
   148→  const targetRed = Number.parseInt(targetColor.slice(1, 3), 16)
   149→  const targetGreen = Number.parseInt(targetColor.slice(3, 5), 16)
   150→  const targetBlue = Number.parseInt(targetColor.slice(5, 7), 16)
   151→
   152→  // Calculate increments for each color channel
   153→  const redIncrement = (targetRed - startRed) / step
   154→  const greenIncrement = (targetGreen - startGreen) / step
   155→  const blueIncrement = (targetBlue - startBlue) / step
   156→
   157→  const transitionColors: string[] = []
   158→
   159→  // Generate transition colors
   160→  for (let i = 0; i < step; i++) {
   161→    // Calculate transition color values
   162→    const transitionRed = Math.round(startRed + redIncrement * i)
   163→    const transitionGreen = Math.round(startGreen + greenIncrement * i)
   164→    const transitionBlue = Math.round(startBlue + blueIncrement * i)
   165→
   166→    // Convert RGB values to hex format
   167→    const hexColor = `#${(
   168→      (1 << 24) |
   169→      (transitionRed << 16) |
   170→      (transitionGreen << 8) |
   171→      transitionBlue
   172→    )
   173→      .toString(16)
   174→      .slice(1)}`
   175→
   176→    // Add transition color to the result array
   177→    transitionColors.push(hexColor)
   178→  }
   179→
   180→  return Array.from(new Set(transitionColors))
   181→}
   182→
   183→export const hexToRgbString = (hex: string) => {
   184→  const match = hex.replace(/^#/, '').match(/.{1,2}/g)
   185→  if (!match) {
   186→    throw new Error('Invalid hex color')
   187→  }
   188→
   189→  const [r, g, b] = match.map((x) => Number.parseInt(x, 16))
   190→  return `${r} ${g} ${b}`
   191→}
   192→
   193→export const isHexColor = (color: string) => {
   194→  return /^#[\da-f]{6}$/i.test(color)
   195→}
   196→
   197→export const isRGBColor = (color: string) => {
   198→  return /^rgb\((?:\d{1,3},\s*){2}\d{1,3}\)$/.test(color)
   199→}
   200→export const isRGBAColor = (color: string) => {
   201→  return /^rgba\((?:\d{1,3},\s*){3}(?:0?\.\d+|1(?:\.0+)?)\)$/.test(
   202→    color,
   203→  )
   204→}
   205→
   206→export const withOpacity = (color: string, opacity: number) => {
   207→  switch (true) {
   208→    case isHexColor(color): {
   209→      // Convert decimal opacity to hex (0-255)
   210→      const alpha = Math.round(opacity * 255)
   211→        .toString(16)
   212→        .padStart(2, '0')
   213→      return `${color}${alpha}`
   214→    }
   215→    case isRGBColor(color): {
   216→      const [r, g, b] = color.match(/\d+/g)!.map(Number)
   217→      return `rgba(${r}, ${g}, ${b}, ${opacity})`
   218→    }
   219→    case isRGBAColor(color): {
   220→      const [r, g, b] = color.match(/\d+/g)!.map(Number)
   221→      return `rgba(${r}, ${g}, ${b}, ${opacity})`
   222→    }
   223→    default: {
   224→      return color
   225→    }
   226→  }
   227→}
   228→export const rgbStringToRgb = (hex: string) => {
   229→  const [r, g, b, a] = hex.split(' ').map((s) => Number.parseFloat(s))
   230→  return `rgba(${r}, ${g}, ${b}, ${a || 1})`
   231→}
   232→
   233→export const getLuminance = (hexColor: string) => {
   234→  const rgb = Number.parseInt(hexColor.replace('#', ''), 16)
   235→  const r = (rgb >> 16) & 0xFF
   236→  const g = (rgb >> 8) & 0xFF
   237→  const b = (rgb >> 0) & 0xFF
   238→  return (0.299 * r + 0.587 * g + 0.114 * b) / 255
   239→}
   240→

     1→const getRandomColor = (
     2→  lightness: [number, number],
     3→  saturation: [number, number],
     4→  hue: number,
     5→) => {
     6→  const satAccent = Math.floor(
     7→    Math.random() * (saturation[1] - saturation[0] + 1) + saturation[0],
     8→  )
     9→  const lightAccent = Math.floor(
    10→    Math.random() * (lightness[1] - lightness[0] + 1) + lightness[0],
    11→  )
    12→
    13→  // Generate the background color by increasing the lightness and decreasing the saturation
    14→  const satBackground = satAccent > 30 ? satAccent - 30 : 0
    15→  const lightBackground = lightAccent < 80 ? lightAccent + 20 : 100
    16→
    17→  return {
    18→    accent: `hsl(${hue}, ${satAccent}%, ${lightAccent}%)`,
    19→    background: `hsl(${hue}, ${satBackground}%, ${lightBackground}%)`,
    20→  }
    21→}

    23→export function stringToHue(str: string) {
    24→  let hash = 0
    25→  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
    26→    hash = str.charCodeAt(i) + ((hash << 5) - hash)
    27→  }
    28→  const hue = hash % 360
    29→  return hue < 0 ? hue + 360 : hue
    30→}
    31→
    32→export const getColorScheme = (hue?: number) => {
    33→  const baseHue = hue ?? Math.floor(Math.random() * 361)
    34→  const complementaryHue = (baseHue + 180) % 360
    35→
    36→  // For light theme, we limit the lightness between 40 and 70 to avoid too bright colors for accent
    37→  const lightColors = getRandomColor([40, 70], [70, 90], baseHue)
    38→
    39→  // For dark theme, we limit the lightness between 20 and 50 to avoid too dark colors for accent
    40→  const darkColors = getRandomColor([20, 50], [70, 90], complementaryHue)
    41→
    42→  return {
    43→    light: {
    44→      accent: lightColors.accent,
    45→      background: lightColors.background,
    46→    },
    47→    dark: {
    48→      accent: darkColors.accent,
    49→      background: darkColors.background,
    50→    },
    51→  }
    52→}
    53→export function addAlphaToHex(hex: string, alpha: number): string {
    54→  if (!/^#(?:[\da-f]{3}){1,2}$/i.test(hex)) {
    55→    throw new Error('Invalid hex color value')
    56→  }
    57→
    58→  let color = ''
    59→  if (hex.length === 4) {
    60→    color = `#${[1, 2, 3]
    61→      .map(
    62→        (index) =>
    63→          Number.parseInt(hex.charAt(index), 16).toString(16) +
    64→          Number.parseInt(hex.charAt(index), 16).toString(16),
    65→      )
    66→      .join('')}`
    67→  } else {
    68→    color = hex
    69→  }
    70→
    71→  const r = Number.parseInt(color.slice(1, 3), 16)
    72→  const g = Number.parseInt(color.slice(3, 5), 16)
    73→  const b = Number.parseInt(color.slice(5, 7), 16)
    74→
    75→  return `rgba(${r},${g},${b},${alpha})`
    76→}
    77→
    78→export function addAlphaToHSL(hsl: string, alpha: number): string {
    79→  if (!/^hsl\(\d{1,3}(?:,\s*[\d.]+%){2}\)$/.test(hsl)) {
    80→    throw new Error('Invalid HSL color value')
    81→  }
    82→
    83→  const hsla = `${hsl.slice(0, -1)}, ${alpha})`
    84→  return hsla.replace('hsl', 'hsla')
    85→}
    86→
    87→export function hexToHsl(hex: string) {
    88→  // Remove the '#' symbol from the hex code
    89→  hex = hex.replace('#', '')
    90→
    91→  // Convert hex values to RGB
    92→  const r = Number.parseInt(hex.slice(0, 2), 16) / 255
    93→  const g = Number.parseInt(hex.slice(2, 4), 16) / 255
    94→  const b = Number.parseInt(hex.slice(4, 6), 16) / 255
    95→
    96→  // Find the minimum and maximum values among R, G, and B
    97→  const min = Math.min(r, g, b)
    98→  const max = Math.max(r, g, b)
    99→
   100→  // Calculate the hue
   101→  let h = 0
   102→  switch (max) {
   103→    case min: {
   104→      h = 0 // No hue for achromatic colors
   105→
   106→      break
   107→    }
   108→    case r: {
   109→      h = ((g - b) / (max - min)) % 6
   110→
   111→      break
   112→    }
   113→    case g: {
   114→      h = (2 + (b - r) / (max - min)) % 6
   115→
   116→      break
   117→    }
   118→    default: {
   119→      h = (4 + (r - g) / (max - min)) % 6
   120→    }
   121→  }
   122→  h = Math.round(h * 60)
   123→
   124→  // Calculate the lightness
   125→  const l = (max + min) / 2
   126→
   127→  // Calculate the saturation
   128→  let s = 0
   129→  if (max !== min) {
   130→    s = (max - min) / (1 - Math.abs(2 * l - 1))
   131→  }
   132→  s = Math.round(s * 100)
   133→
   134→  // Return the HSL values as a string
   135→  return [h, s, Math.round(l * 100)]
   136→}
   137→
   138→export function generateTransitionColors(
   139→  startColor: string,
   140→  targetColor: string,
   141→  step: number,
   142→): string[] {
   143→  // Convert startColor and targetColor to RGB values
   144→  const startRed = Number.parseInt(startColor.slice(1, 3), 16)
   145→  const startGreen = Number.parseInt(startColor.slice(3, 5), 16)
   146→  const startBlue = Number.parseInt(startColor.slice(5, 7), 16)
   147→
   148→  const targetRed = Number.parseInt(targetColor.slice(1, 3), 16)
   149→  const targetGreen = Number.parseInt(targetColor.slice(3, 5), 16)
   150→  const targetBlue = Number.parseInt(targetColor.slice(5, 7), 16)
   151→
   152→  // Calculate increments for each color channel
   153→  const redIncrement = (targetRed - startRed) / step
   154→  const greenIncrement = (targetGreen - startGreen) / step
   155→  const blueIncrement = (targetBlue - startBlue) / step
   156→
   157→  const transitionColors: string[] = []
   158→
   159→  // Generate transition colors
   160→  for (let i = 0; i < step; i++) {
   161→    // Calculate transition color values
   162→    const transitionRed = Math.round(startRed + redIncrement * i)
   163→    const transitionGreen = Math.round(startGreen + greenIncrement * i)
   164→    const transitionBlue = Math.round(startBlue + blueIncrement * i)
   165→
   166→    // Convert RGB values to hex format
   167→    const hexColor = `#${(
   168→      (1 << 24) |
   169→      (transitionRed << 16) |
   170→      (transitionGreen << 8) |
   171→      transitionBlue
   172→    )
   173→      .toString(16)
   174→      .slice(1)}`
   175→
   176→    // Add transition color to the result array
   177→    transitionColors.push(hexColor)
   178→  }
   179→
   180→  return Array.from(new Set(transitionColors))
   181→}
   182→
   183→export const hexToRgbString = (hex: string) => {
   184→  const match = hex.replace(/^#/, '').match(/.{1,2}/g)
   185→  if (!match) {
   186→    throw new Error('Invalid hex color')
   187→  }
   188→
   189→  const [r, g, b] = match.map((x) => Number.parseInt(x, 16))
   190→  return `${r} ${g} ${b}`
   191→}
   192→
   193→export const isHexColor = (color: string) => {
   194→  return /^#[\da-f]{6}$/i.test(color)
   195→}
   196→
   197→export const isRGBColor = (color: string) => {
   198→  return /^rgb\((?:\d{1,3},\s*){2}\d{1,3}\)$/.test(color)
   199→}
   200→export const isRGBAColor = (color: string) => {
   201→  return /^rgba\((?:\d{1,3},\s*){3}(?:0?\.\d+|1(?:\.0+)?)\)$/.test(
   202→    color,
   203→  )
   204→}
   205→
   206→export const withOpacity = (color: string, opacity: number) => {
   207→  switch (true) {
   208→    case isHexColor(color): {
   209→      // Convert decimal opacity to hex (0-255)
   210→      const alpha = Math.round(opacity * 255)
   211→        .toString(16)
   212→        .padStart(2, '0')
   213→      return `${color}${alpha}`
   214→    }
   215→    case isRGBColor(color): {
   216→      const [r, g, b] = color.match(/\d+/g)!.map(Number)
   217→      return `rgba(${r}, ${g}, ${b}, ${opacity})`
   218→    }
   219→    case isRGBAColor(color): {
   220→      const [r, g, b] = color.match(/\d+/g)!.map(Number)
   221→      return `rgba(${r}, ${g}, ${b}, ${opacity})`
   222→    }
   223→    default: {
   224→      return color
   225→    }
   226→  }
   227→}
   228→export const rgbStringToRgb = (hex: string) => {
   229→  const [r, g, b, a] = hex.split(' ').map((s) => Number.parseFloat(s))
   230→  return `rgba(${r}, ${g}, ${b}, ${a || 1})`
   231→}
   232→
   233→export const getLuminance = (hexColor: string) => {
   234→  const rgb = Number.parseInt(hexColor.replace('#', ''), 16)
   235→  const r = (rgb >> 16) & 0xFF
   236→  const g = (rgb >> 8) & 0xFF
   237→  const b = (rgb >> 0) & 0xFF
   238→  return (0.299 * r + 0.587 * g + 0.114 * b) / 255
   239→}

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>

<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```tsx
import { useRendererMode } from '@haklex/rich-editor';
import type { TagRendererProps } from '@haklex/rich-editor/static';
import { getTagBgColor, TagRenderer } from '@haklex/rich-editor/static';
import {
  ActionBar,
  ActionButton,
  Popover,
  PopoverPanel,
  PopoverTrigger,
} from '@haklex/rich-editor-ui';
import { useLexicalComposerContext } from '@lexical/react/LexicalComposerContext';
import { $getNearestNodeFromDOMNode } from 'lexical';
import { Tag, Trash2 } from 'lucide-react';
import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';

export function TagEditRenderer(props: TagRendererProps) {
  const mode = useRendererMode();

  if (mode !== 'editor') {
    return <TagRenderer {...props} />;
  }

  return <TagEditRendererInner {...props} />;
}

function TagEditRendererInner({ text }: TagRendererProps) {
  const [editor] = useLexicalComposerContext();
  const editable = editor.isEditable();
  const wrapperRef = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);

  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [editText, setEditText] = useState(text);

  useEffect(() => {
    setEditText(text);
  }, [text]);

  const commitChanges = useCallback(() => {
    const trimmed = editText.trim();
    if (!trimmed) return;
    if (!wrapperRef.current) return;

    editor.update(() => {
      const node = $getNearestNodeFromDOMNode(wrapperRef.current!);
      if (!node) return;
      const writable = node.getWritable() as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
      writable.__text = trimmed;
    });
    setOpen(false);
  }, [editor, editText]);

  const handleDelete = useCallback(() => {
    if (!wrapperRef.current) return;

    editor.update(() => {
      const node = $getNearestNodeFromDOMNode(wrapperRef.current!);
      if (node) node.remove();
    });
    setOpen(false);
  }, [editor]);

  const handleKeyDown = useCallback(
    (e: React.KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (e.key === 'Enter') {
        e.preventDefault();
        commitChanges();
      } else if (e.key === 'Escape') {
        e.preventDefault();
        setEditText(text);
        setOpen(false);
      }
    },
    [commitChanges, text],
  );

  if (!editable) {
    return <TagRenderer text={text} />;
  }

  return (
    <Popover
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={(nextOpen: boolean) => {
        setOpen(nextOpen);
        if (!nextOpen) setEditText(text);
      }}
    >
      <PopoverTrigger
        nativeButton={false}
        render={
          <span
            ref={wrapperRef}
            style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', cursor: 'pointer' }}
          />
        }
      >
        <span className="rich-tag" style={{ backgroundColor: getTagBgColor(editText) }}>
          {text}
        </span>
      </PopoverTrigger>
      <PopoverPanel side="bottom" sideOffset={8}>
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 8, padding: 12, width: 240 }}>
          <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
            <Tag size={14} style={{ flexShrink: 0, opacity: 0.5 }} />
            <input
              autoFocus
              placeholder="Tag text"
              style={{
                flex: 1,
                appearance: 'none',
                border: 'none',
                backgroundColor: 'transparent',
                color: 'inherit',
                fontSize: 'inherit',
                padding: 0,
                outline: 'none',
                minWidth: 0,
              }}
              type="text"
              value={editText}
              onBlur={commitChanges}
              onChange={(e) => setEditText(e.target.value)}
              onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}
            />
          </div>
          <ActionBar>
            <ActionButton danger onClick={handleDelete}>
              <Trash2 size={14} />
              Remove
            </ActionButton>
          </ActionBar>
        </div>
      </PopoverPanel>
    </Popover>
  );
}
```

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The user wants the tag editing to be inline, similar to how inline code editing works, rather than using a popover. This makes more sense for a tag - just clicking on it to edit text in place.

Let me think about how to implement inline editing for the tag. The tag is a DecoratorNode, which renders as a React component. To make it editable inline, I could:

1. When clicked, replace the tag text with an input field that's styled to look like the tag
2. On blur/enter, commit the changes

Actually, looking at how other editors handle this, a contenteditable span or a simple input that appears in-place would be best.

I'll go with a straightforward click-to-edit pattern where the tag switches between a display state and an editable input field, with Enter or blur saving the changes and Escape canceling them.

</details></think>

```tsx
import { useRendererMode } from '@haklex/rich-editor';
import type { TagRendererProps } from '@haklex/rich-editor/static';
import { getTagBgColor, TagRenderer } from '@haklex/rich-editor/static';
import { useLexicalComposerContext } from '@lexical/react/LexicalComposerContext';
import { $getNearestNodeFromDOMNode } from 'lexical';
import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';

export function TagEditRenderer(props: TagRendererProps) {
  const mode = useRendererMode();

  if (mode !== 'editor') {
    return <TagRenderer {...props} />;
  }

  return <TagEditRendererInner {...props} />;
}

function TagEditRendererInner({ text }: TagRendererProps) {
  const [editor] = useLexicalComposerContext();
  const editable = editor.isEditable();
  const wrapperRef = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);
  const inputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);

  const [editing, setEditing] = useState(false);
  const [editText, setEditText] = useState(text);

  useEffect(() => {
    setEditText(text);
  }, [text]);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (editing) {
      // Defer focus to next frame so Lexical doesn't steal it
      requestAnimationFrame(() => inputRef.current?.focus());
    }
  }, [editing]);

  const commitChanges = useCallback(() => {
    const trimmed = editText.trim();
    if (!trimmed || trimmed === text) {
      setEditText(text);
      setEditing(false);
      return;
    }
    if (!wrapperRef.current) return;

    editor.update(() => {
      const node = $getNearestNodeFromDOMNode(wrapperRef.current!);
      if (!node) return;
      const writable = node.getWritable() as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
      writable.__text = trimmed;
    });
    setEditing(false);
  }, [editor, editText, text]);

  const handleKeyDown = useCallback(
    (e: React.KeyboardEvent) => {
      e.stopPropagation();
      if (e.key === 'Enter') {
        e.preventDefault();
        commitChanges();
      } else if (e.key === 'Escape') {
        e.preventDefault();
        setEditText(text);
        setEditing(false);
      }
    },
    [commitChanges, text],
  );

  if (!editable) {
    return <TagRenderer text={text} />;
  }

  const bgColor = getTagBgColor(editing ? editText : text);

  if (editing) {
    return (
      <span
        className="rich-tag"
        ref={wrapperRef}
        style={{ backgroundColor: bgColor, display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center' }}
      >
        <input
          ref={inputRef}
          style={{
            appearance: 'none',
            border: 'none',
            backgroundColor: 'transparent',
            color: 'inherit',
            font: 'inherit',
            fontSize: 'inherit',
            lineHeight: 'inherit',
            padding: 0,
            margin: 0,
            outline: 'none',
            width: `${Math.max(editText.length, 1)}ch`,
            minWidth: '2ch',
          }}
          type="text"
          value={editText}
          onBlur={commitChanges}
          onChange={(e) => setEditText(e.target.value)}
          onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}
          onMouseDown={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
        />
      </span>
    );
  }

  return (
    <span
      className="rich-tag"
      ref={wrapperRef}
      style={{ backgroundColor: bgColor, cursor: 'pointer' }}
      onClick={(e) => {
        e.preventDefault();
        e.stopPropagation();
        setEditing(true);
      }}
    >
      {text}
    </span>
  );
}
```

Release @haklex/\* packages and update all downstream consumers.

## Steps

### 1. Pre-flight checks

Run `git status` in haklex repo. Ensure working tree is clean or all changes are committed. If not, stop and ask the user.

### 2. Version bump

Read current version from `packages/rich-editor/package.json` → `version` field. Default to patch bump (increment the last segment). Run:

```bash
pnpm bumpp --no-git --no-tag < patch_version > -r
```

After bumpp completes, read the new version from `packages/rich-editor/package.json` → `version` field. Store as `$NEW_VERSION`.

### 3. Build & Publish

```bash
cd < HOME > /git/repos/haklex && pnpm build:packages && pnpm -r publish --no-git-checks --filter '@haklex/*' --filter '!@haklex/rich-editor-demo'
```

`build:packages` only builds workspace packages under `packages/`; the dev playground now lives in top-level `demo/` and remains excluded from publish.

If publish fails, stop and report.

### 4. Commit and push the version bump in haklex

Stage and commit all changed `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` files:

```
release: v$NEW_VERSION
```

Then push to remote:

```bash
git push
```

### 5. Update downstream projects

For each downstream project, update all `@haklex/*` dependency versions to `$NEW_VERSION`:

**Shiroi** — `<HOME>/git/repos/Shiroi/apps/web/package.json`

- Update `@haklex/rich-editor`, `@haklex/rich-kit-shiro`, `@haklex/rich-static-renderer`

**admin-vue3** — `<HOME>/git/repos/admin-vue3/package.json`

- Update `@haklex/rich-diff`, `@haklex/rich-ext-nested-doc`, `@haklex/rich-editor`, `@haklex/rich-editor-ui`, `@haklex/rich-kit-shiro`, `@haklex/rich-plugin-toolbar`, `@haklex/rich-style-token`

**mx-core** — `<HOME>/git/repos/mx-core/apps/core/package.json`

- Update `@haklex/rich-headless`

Use sed or Edit to replace pinned version strings. Match pattern: `"@haklex/<pkg>": "<old_version>"` → `"@haklex/<pkg>": "$NEW_VERSION"`.

### 6. Install in downstream projects

Run `pnpm install` in each downstream project root:

```bash
cd < HOME > /git/repos/Shiroi && pnpm install
cd < HOME > /git/repos/admin-vue3 && pnpm install
cd < HOME > /git/repos/mx-core && pnpm install
```

### 7. Check for new features to integrate

Compare the haklex git log since the previous version tag to identify new exports, new packages, or breaking changes:

```bash
cd < HOME > /git/repos/haklex && git log --oneline HEAD~20..HEAD
```

Scan for:

- New package exports (new entry points in `package.json` exports)
- New renderer/plugin/extension packages that downstream projects might want
- Breaking changes (renamed exports, removed APIs)

If new features are found, ask the user whether to integrate them into specific downstream projects. Do NOT auto-integrate without confirmation.

### 8. Commit and push in downstream projects

For each downstream project with changes, stage, commit, and push immediately:

```bash
# Shiroi
cd < HOME > /git/repos/Shiroi && git add -A && git commit -m "chore(deps): bump @haklex/* to $NEW_VERSION" && git push

# admin-vue3
cd < HOME > /git/repos/admin-vue3 && git add -A && git commit -m "chore(deps): bump @haklex/* to $NEW_VERSION" && git push

# mx-core
cd < HOME > /git/repos/mx-core && git add -A && git commit -m "chore(deps): bump @haklex/* to $NEW_VERSION" && git push
```

### 9. Summary

Print a table:
| Project | Version | Packages Updated | New Features |

     5→
     6→import {

    18→// eslint-disable-next-line regexp/no-useless-assertions -- intentionally never-matching regex for export-only transformers
    19→const NEVER = /a^/;
    20→const NOOP = () => {};
    21→
    22→function qA(v: string): string {
    23→  return v.replaceAll('"', '\\"');
    24→}
    25→
    26→function escHtml(v: string): string {
    27→  return v.replaceAll('&', '&amp;').replaceAll('<', '&lt;').replaceAll('>', '&gt;');
    28→}
    29→
    30→function escCell(v: string): string {
    31→  return v.replaceAll('|', '\\|').replaceAll('\n', '<br/>');
    32→}
    33→
    34→function fence(content: string): string {
    35→  const m = content.match(/`+/g);
    36→  const max = m?.reduce((a, r) => Math.max(a, r.length), 0) ?? 0;
    37→  return '`'.repeat(Math.max(3, max + 1));
    38→}
    39→
    40→function walkText(node: Record<string, unknown>): string {
    41→  const children = node.children as Record<string, unknown>[] | undefined;
    42→  if (!children) return (node.text as string) ?? '';
    43→  return children.map(walkText).join('\n');
    44→}

    47→  if (!state || typeof state !== 'object') return '';

Since they are different class instances, `$isCodeNode()` returns `false`.

This means the standard `CODE` transformer never matches the legacy code node, so it falls through to default text extraction and outputs just `x=1` without the fenced code block formatting. The issue probably existed before v0.0.72, but the test was likely added to validate the upgrade. I'm creating a LEGACY_CODE_NODE_TRANSFORMER that checks for the 'code' type and extracts the text content and language property, then wraps it in fence markers. Release @haklex/\* packages and update all downstream consumers.

## Steps

### 1. Pre-flight checks

Run `git status` in haklex repo. Ensure working tree is clean or all changes are committed. If not, stop and ask the user.

### 2. Version bump

Read current version from `packages/rich-editor/package.json` → `version` field. Default to patch bump (increment the last segment). Run:

```bash
pnpm bumpp --no-git --no-tag < patch_version > -r
```

After bumpp completes, read the new version from `packages/rich-editor/package.json` → `version` field. Store as `$NEW_VERSION`.

### 3. Build & Publish

```bash
cd < HOME > /git/repos/haklex && pnpm build:packages && pnpm -r publish --no-git-checks --filter '@haklex/*' --filter '!@haklex/rich-editor-demo'
```

`build:packages` only builds workspace packages under `packages/`; the dev playground now lives in top-level `demo/` and remains excluded from publish.

If publish fails, stop and report.

### 4. Commit and push the version bump in haklex

Stage and commit all changed `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` files:

```
release: v$NEW_VERSION
```

Then push to remote:

```bash
git push
```

### 5. Update downstream projects

For each downstream project, update all `@haklex/*` dependency versions to `$NEW_VERSION`:

**Shiroi** — `<HOME>/git/repos/Shiroi/apps/web/package.json`

- Update `@haklex/rich-editor`, `@haklex/rich-kit-shiro`, `@haklex/rich-static-renderer`

**admin-vue3** — `<HOME>/git/repos/admin-vue3/package.json`

- Update `@haklex/rich-diff`, `@haklex/rich-ext-nested-doc`, `@haklex/rich-editor`, `@haklex/rich-editor-ui`, `@haklex/rich-kit-shiro`, `@haklex/rich-plugin-toolbar`, `@haklex/rich-style-token`

**mx-core** — `<HOME>/git/repos/mx-core/apps/core/package.json`

- Update `@haklex/rich-headless`

Use sed or Edit to replace pinned version strings. Match pattern: `"@haklex/<pkg>": "<old_version>"` → `"@haklex/<pkg>": "$NEW_VERSION"`.

### 6. Install in downstream projects

Run `pnpm install` in each downstream project root:

```bash
cd < HOME > /git/repos/Shiroi && pnpm install
cd < HOME > /git/repos/admin-vue3 && pnpm install
cd < HOME > /git/repos/mx-core && pnpm install
```

### 7. Check for new features to integrate

Compare the haklex git log since the previous version tag to identify new exports, new packages, or breaking changes:

```bash
cd < HOME > /git/repos/haklex && git log --oneline HEAD~20..HEAD
```

Scan for:

- New package exports (new entry points in `package.json` exports)
- New renderer/plugin/extension packages that downstream projects might want
- Breaking changes (renamed exports, removed APIs)

If new features are found, ask the user whether to integrate them into specific downstream projects. Do NOT auto-integrate without confirmation.

### 8. Commit and push in downstream projects

For each downstream project with changes, stage, commit, and push immediately:

```bash
# Shiroi
cd < HOME > /git/repos/Shiroi && git add -A && git commit -m "chore(deps): bump @haklex/* to $NEW_VERSION" && git push

# admin-vue3
cd < HOME > /git/repos/admin-vue3 && git add -A && git commit -m "chore(deps): bump @haklex/* to $NEW_VERSION" && git push

# mx-core
cd < HOME > /git/repos/mx-core && git add -A && git commit -m "chore(deps): bump @haklex/* to $NEW_VERSION" && git push
```
